candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Uses and gratifications statements regarding newspapers produce three distinct groups (surveillance, diversion, interaction) and predict weekday and Sunday newspaper readership
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, 'Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications,' Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Newspaper uses-and-gratifications statements produce three distinct factors: surveillance, diversion, and interaction.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: The replication found two factors rather than the original three and explicitly stated that Hypothesis 1 could not be accepted. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Weekday newspaper subscribers are strongly oriented toward obtaining immediate knowledge of big news events.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: The authors described this hypothesis as strongly supported, but the result was only marginally significant at the .15 level and was characterized in the Discussion as marginal at best. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Weekday single-copy newspaper readers are strongly oriented toward finding interesting or unusual stories to tell others.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: The authors stated that this hypothesis disappeared and received no support in the replication. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Weekday newspaper non-readers are strongly oriented toward using a newspaper simply to pass the time.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: The authors stated that this hypothesis disappeared and received no support in the replication. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Sunday newspaper subscribers are oriented toward immediate knowledge of big news events, being happy, and obtaining more information about events they have seen.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: Only the immediate-knowledge component received support; the hypothesized relations involving being happy and obtaining more information disappeared. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Sunday single-copy readers are oriented toward understanding what is going on and toward using the newspaper simply to pass the time.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: The replication authors explicitly stated that the results clearly supported Hypothesis 6, although the reported pattern combined Sunday non-readers with the hypothesis wording. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications
candidates.description: Sunday newspaper non-readers are oriented toward passing the time and toward obtaining more information about events they have seen.
candidates.citation_sentence: Wayne M. Towers, "Weekday and Sunday Readership Seen Through Uses and Gratifications," Newspaper Research Journal 6:20-32 (1985).
candidates.notes: The replication found the predicted pattern for Sunday non-readers, but the paper's hypothesis numbering and summary inconsistently attribute this support to Hypothesis 6 and describe the overall Sunday results as limited or mixed.
